_status_note: The word is the TEST OUTCOME, not a verdict on argus. A dashboard that
labels a product 'unsafe' on the strength of assertions its maintainers
have not agreed to is overstepping -- E5 and E9 encode what this suite
thinks argus should do, and that question is open. The severity lives in
the risk number, the class counts and the sentence, all of which describe
what was observed rather than what to conclude.

glossary.open: argus reported success without actually running the check. Nothing warns you, so unscanned code can ship looking approved.
glossary.closed: argus stopped or errored when it should have worked. Your pipeline blocks, which is disruptive, but nothing slips past unnoticed.
glossary.degraded: Something alongside the scan broke, such as uploading a report. The scan itself ran and the gate still held, so nothing unsafe got through.

open.line: 2 tests report success without scanning — see E5, E9

closed.line: argus refuses to run where it should work

degraded.line: an auxiliary path is broken; scans and gates still work

none.line: every defined test that ran, passed

index.name: Risk index
index.caveat: The weights are a judgement call, not a measurement. The number adds up rather than averaging, so adding passing tests can never lower it. Only fixing a failure does.

_why_open: R6, C3-C6, D3, D4, E8, S13, S14 and S18 all assert that argus FAILS a run:
a severity gate firing, a build gate firing, missing registry credentials
being rejected, an SCN category threshold being enforced. If one of them
goes red, argus let through something it was asked to stop -- the
E5 and E9 are the same class observed directly: a scan naming no
recognised scanner, and a remote scan with an empty image_ref, both report
_why_degraded: E11 and E14 are SARIF upload paths: losing them costs visibility in the
Security tab, not the scan itself. S16 is dry-run issue payloads, S25 the
optional AI fallback, U4 the SCN detector's own unit tests -- all real, none
of them a control a consumer is relying on at scan time.
